## How I arrived at this number:

**Step 1 – Total living giraffes:**
The most recent IUCN/consensus estimates place the global wild giraffe population at roughly **117,000** individuals (across the four recognized species and seven subspecies). Adding giraffes in zoos and private collections (~1,500–2,000) brings the total to approximately **119,000**.

**Step 2 – Spots per giraffe:**
The dark patches (what most people call "spots"; they're actually dark brown/umber rather than truly black) cover the neck, torso, and legs. A rough count from photographs:

| Region | Approx. patches |
|---|---|
| Body (both sides) | 80 – 120 |
| Neck | 30 – 50 |
| Legs (all four) | 25 – 45 |
| Head | 5 – 10 |
| **Total** | **~200** |

I'll use **≈ 200 patches** as the per-giraffe average (reticulated giraffes have slightly fewer, larger patches; Masai giraffes slightly more, smaller ones – it roughly balances).

**Step 3 – Multiply:**
119,000 giraffes × 200 spots ≈ **23,800,000**, which I round to **23,000,000** as a clean point estimate.
